rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (Tenants' Right to Know Regulations) – just cause, relocation assistance, buyouts
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy without just cause, either at-fault (e.g. nonpayment, material lease breach, nuisance, waste, criminal activity) or no-fault (owner or relative move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, government or court orders to vacate, demolition or substantial remodel). No-fault terminations need 30 or 60 days' written notice (per Civ. Code § 1946.1) in at least 12-point font, stating the basis, the relocation assistance and the right to re-rent. The landlord must give relocation assistance of 2 months' rent (3 months if the tenant is a senior or disabled), paid directly within 15 days of the notice or taken as a rent waiver. Notice to the Housing Commission is due within 3 business days, but only after the Commission opens a submission portal. A tenant displaced by a no-fault termination under (b)(1), (3) or (4) has a right of first offer for 5 years. Landlords must give all covered tenants a protections notice and the Tenant Protection Guide. Buyout offers require a prior written disclosure and a compliant written agreement for more than the relocation amount. Retaliation is prohibited. Non-compliance voids the termination notice.
rules.key_value: No-fault: relocation of 2 months' rent (3 months for senior/disabled), paid within 15 days or as rent waiver; 30/60-day notice; 5-year right to re-rent offer (30 days to accept); remedies of at least 3x actual economic damages for wrongful eviction and at least 3x required relocation assistance plus actual damages; at-fault: written notice to cure then 3-day notice to quit

new_construction_exemption.basis: certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (not applicable to mobilehomes)

unverifiable_exemptions: Housing restricted by deed, regulatory agreement or other document as affordable housing for very low, low or moderate income households
Housing subject to an affordable housing subsidy agreement (Section 8 not exempt)

Separately alienable residential property (including mobilehomes) whose landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member or mobilehome park management and where the tenants were given the required written exemption notice
Housing in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, adult residential facilities, or non-profit transitional housing
Dormitories owned and operated by higher education or K-12 institutions
Property where tenant shares bathroom or kitchen with a landlord who lives there as principal residence
Owner-occupied single-family residence renting no more than two bedrooms, two ADUs or two JADUs, or a duplex where the landlord occupies one unit
coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental properties (tenancies over 30 days) in San Diego, except housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years and the listed exempt categories.
coverage.owner_conditions: Exempt: single-family residence occupied by the landlord as principal residence (renting no more than two bedrooms, two ADUs or two JADUs); duplex where landlord occupies one unit as principal residence at the start of the tenancy and continues to; separately alienable property whose landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member or mobilehome park management and which gave the required written notice.
coverage.other_conditions: Mobilehomes under the Mobilehome Residency Law, transient/tourist hotel and short-term residential occupancy are exempt. Mobilehomes are excluded from the 15-year new construction exemption.

rules.exemptions: Division does not apply to: transient/tourist hotel and short-term residential occupancy; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (Section 8 excluded from the exemption); mobilehomes under the Mobilehome Residency Law; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended care, residential care facility for the elderly, adult residential facility, non-profit transitional housing; dormitories; shared-facility rentals with a resident landlord; owner-occupied single-family residences and duplexes; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years; separately alienable property with a qualifying non-corporate landlord who gave written notice.
rules.effective_date_note: Division retitled and substantially amended by O-21647 N.S., adopted 5-25-2023, effective 6-24-2023. Further amended by O-21769 N.S. on 2-27-2024, effective 3-28-2024. The original Tenants' Right to Know Regulations were added 3-30-2004 by O-19269 N.S. The enacted date is taken from the 'added 5-25-2023' history note.
citation_aliases: S.D. Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause.
rules.review_note: Per-section commission-notice requirements (§ 98.0706(a)(2), (b)(2)) are deferred until 30 days after the Housing Commission announces a submission portal. Relocation assistance (§ 98.0706(c)) and buyouts (§ 98.0707) are folded into this record because they are subsections of the same Division.
rules.source_notes: Official municipal code text (3-2024 version). No later amendments after O-21769 N.S. are reflected.

result.doc_summary: San Diego Municipal Code Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7 (Residential Tenant Protections, formerly Tenants' Right to Know) requires just cause to terminate covered tenancies. It lists at-fault and no-fault causes, with notice content, relocation assistance of 2 months' rent (3 for seniors or disabled tenants), a 5-year right to re-rent, buyout agreement rules, anti-retaliation protection and remedies of at least 3x damages. It exempts the 15-year-new-construction housing and various owner-occupied, affordable, institutional and similar categories. The document does not address rent caps, deposits, screening fees or screening restrictions, or algorithmic rent-setting.
